title: PRD: Autorepair & Safety Harness for KV Cache Regeneration
creator: Maya Fernandez
description:
Summary: After the Feb 2025 KV cache regeneration incident we need a set of concrete PRD updates that convert postmortem action items into development requirements and acceptance criteria. The goal is to ensure automated detection and safe remediation (autorepair) of KV cache inconsistencies, formalize rollback and circuit-breaker contracts, and add synthetic verification so regressions are caught before customer impact.

Background: The incident showed a gap between runtime heuristics for cache regen and operational tooling: manually invoked cache repairs sometimes caused prolonged degraded throughput and incorrect responses for a small fraction of requests. Postmortem recommended: 1) explicit autorepair flows with safety gates, 2) richer telemetry for regen success/failure, 3) synthetic and canary verification of cache state post-regeneration, 4) automatic rollback triggers tied to SLO degradations.

Goals:
- Define product requirements for an "autorepair" feature that can safely rehydrate KV cache shards with minimal customer impact.
- Specify required observability and SLO gates that must be satisfied before and after autorepair.
- Define rollback and fallback policies (circuit breakers) that runtime and orchestration must implement.
- Add synthetic tests and canary tasks that verify KV cache integrity and performance post-action.

Out of scope: full redesign of KV cache data model, major kernel-level runtime rewrites, cross-region full-data migrations. Those will be tracked in separate engineering epics.

Artifacts: Confluence PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/runtime-kv-autorepair-prd (draft); Postmortem: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident-2025-02-kv-regeneration-postmortem.pdf; Proposed API sketch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache-proposals/pull/12
acceptance_criteria: Autorepair feature documented in PRD with clear ingress points (operator/manual/automatic) and parameterization (max concurrency, rate-limit, shard-selection policy)
Telemetry contract defined: regen-start, regen-success, regen-failure, bytes-rehydrated, per-shard latency and error rates; all emitted to tracing/metrics with dashboard templates
Safety gates defined: autorepair must only run when (a) per-route token error-rate < X, (b) regional capacity headroom > Y, and (c) replica health > 90%

Rollback contract defined: if SLO deviation for latency or correctness exceeds threshold Z for > N minutes during/after regen, system triggers automatic rollback and notifies on-call with runbook link
Synthetic verification harness implemented in staging: end-to-end canary that performs induced cache evictions and validates correctness and latency within defined thresholds within 5 minutes
Runtime APIs for triggering autorepair exposed to console and CLI with audit log entries for each action
E2E acceptance tests added to CI: simulated regen under load, verifying fallback to compatible model variants and no data corruption
Runbook and playbooks updated with explicit post-action checks and owner assignments; runbook invoked automatically on autorepair failures
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive autorepair reduces manual toil but increases risk of regressing serving latency; hence safety gate conservative defaults and gradual rollout required.
Decision: start with region-local autorepair (no cross-region rehydration) to limit blast radius.
Telemetry naming will follow existing metrics conventions (kvcache.regen.*) to make dashboards composable with runtime dashboards.
Fallback preference: prefer model-variant fallback over cache repair if latency breach risk is high during peak traffic. Engineering to provide formalized cost/latency model (ENG-8712).
